bullets.title: GOOGL: Wells Fargo data shows search sessions +35% YoY in 2Q26, holding share vs ChatGPT
bullets.body: Wells Fargo channel data shows global search category session growth accelerated from low-single-digits in 4Q24 to 35% YoY in 2Q26, with Google maintaining market share vs ChatGPT over the past 12 months. Expansion of use cases (including other LLMs pinging Google's index, which don't count against Google sessions) is driving growth. Google now has supply surplus enabling ad load reduction especially in AI search products, a potential monetization lever.

bullets.title: AVGO: +3.7% on Apple ASIC collaboration extension through 2031; mgmt call Tuesday
bullets.body: Broadcom extended its custom ASIC silicon collaboration with Apple through 2031, driving shares up 3.7% on the session. Wolfe Research is hosting an AVGO CEO/CFO virtual group meeting Tuesday at 1pm ET with a wrap-up webcast Wednesday — key catalyst for positioning heading into earnings.

bullets.title: NVDA: Next-gen AI rack system delayed to 2028 on manufacturing issues
bullets.body: Nvidia's next-generation AI rack system has been pushed back to 2028 due to manufacturing challenges with circuit board production. Semiconductors still outperformed on the session with SOX rebounding sharply after an 11%+ two-day drop, driven by AI capex optimism from the WULF/Anthropic infrastructure deal.

bullets.title: WULF: +4.9% on $19B 20-year Anthropic lease at 401MW Justified Data Campus
bullets.body: TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic at its Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, KY generating ~$19B in contracted revenue at 401MW capacity, with initial capacity online H2 2027. Implied rent of $197/kW/month exceeds Citi's prior $150/kW/month estimate; estimated development yield ~18%. Separately, WULF sold a 50.1% stake in Abernathy JV to Fluidstack for $530M (vs. ~$616M DCF value), with Citi maintaining Buy and $36 PT.

bullets.title: IREN: +13% on AI data center capacity demand / Anthropic infrastructure momentum
bullets.body: IREN surged ~13% on the session, benefiting from the broader AI infrastructure capacity narrative catalyzed by the WULF/Anthropic deal news.

bullets.title: FSLR: Deutsche Bank upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $272 from $245 (17% upside)
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank analyst Corinne Blanchard upgraded First Solar to Buy from Hold and raised the price target to $272 from $245, implying ~17% upside. Shares gained ~2% in after-hours trading to ~$238. FactSet consensus PT is $255.45 with range $150-$330.

bullets.title: MSFT: -1.0% on 4,800 Xbox job cuts; analyst buy-rated on underappreciated CoPilot orchestration thesis
bullets.body: Microsoft cut 4,800 jobs primarily from its gaming division with four Xbox studios going independent, pressuring shares -1.0%. Separately, a sell-side analyst reiterates Buy with high conviction, arguing investors underestimate MSFT's CoPilot orchestration layer that routes enterprise queries across AI models — with Azure acceleration and capex deceleration expected at earnings in ~3 weeks.

bullets.title: ANET: +8.3% leading Comm Equipment sub-sector +2.6% on AI networking momentum
bullets.body: Arista Networks led communication equipment stocks with an 8.3% gain as AI networking demand drove the sub-sector up 2.6%. CIEN gained 2.7% on similar dynamics.

bullets.title: WDC: +7.1% as HDD and memory names rebound with SOX
bullets.body: Western Digital gained 7.1% as HDD and memory names led the semiconductor rebound following the SOX's 11%+ two-day decline. MU also benefited from sector momentum and separately signed a long-term semiconductor supply agreement with Ford for vehicles.

bullets.title: DDOG: Downgraded to Market Perform from Outperform at Bernstein, -1.9%
bullets.body: Bernstein downgraded Datadog to Market Perform from Outperform; shares fell 1.9% on the session. Software sub-sector was broadly weak (+0.2%), held back by MSFT, DDOG, ADBE (-0.8%), and CRM (-0.3%).

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi maintains Buy; 2Q26 CCUs +5% YoY, bookings tracking near low-end of guidance
bullets.body: Citi's RoMonitor data shows 2Q26 average peak CCUs of 13.0M, up 5% YoY, implying ~$1.57B in bookings — slightly below the mid-point of company guidance ($1.55-$1.61B) and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.59B. QTD CCUs of 16.3M are down ~7% vs 3Q25. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: CMCSA: -1.7% as Sky agrees to $2.1B ITV acquisition; Minions opening disappoints
bullets.body: Comcast fell 1.7% after its Sky unit agreed to acquire ITV's Media & Entertainment business for $2.1B. Additionally, Minions & Monsters opened to a disappointing $61M weekend box office. Media Conglomerates was the weakest sub-sector at -1.9%.

bullets.title: BE, ENPH, GEV: Renewables outperform as sector rallies sharply
bullets.body: Bloom Energy surged 8.9%, Enphase gained 3.4%, and GE Vernova rose 3.5% as the renewables sector rallied sharply, outperforming the S&P 500 Utilities Index which declined 1.1%. Global X Hydrogen ETF +2.4% and Invesco Solar ETF +2.2%.

bullets.title: AVGO catalyst: Wolfe Research hosting CEO/CFO virtual mgmt meeting Tuesday; wrap-up webcast Wednesday
bullets.body: Wolfe Research has AVGO CEO and CFO virtual group meeting Tuesday at 1pm ET, followed by a wrap-up takeaway webcast Wednesday at 11am ET. Friday's 'Chips with Caso' will also cover AVGO, ASML semi-cap earnings, MU earnings, and QCOM analyst day.

bullets.title: CRWV: Roth QSG fielding customer survey on market share and competitive positioning
bullets.body: Roth Capital's QSG is surveying 100-150 CoreWeave customers and competitors' customers (Vol. 4) to quantify market share, differentiation, satisfaction on speed/performance, and ability to manage overcapacity risks vs. hyperscale AI cloud peers. Results accessible to Roth internet analyst Rohit Kulkarni.

bullets.title: IB deal activity surge: M&A +64% YoY, IPOs +353% YoY in 2Q26; earnings kick off July 14
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's deal dashboard shows broad-based investment banking strength in 2Q26 with announced M&A up 64% YoY (completed +33%), ECM/IPOs up 107%/353% YoY respectively, and DCM up 19%. Earnings season kicks off July 14 with C, GS, JPM, WFC; management expected to reiterate positive deal pipelines.

bullets.title: Fed's Waller turns hawkish: inflation risks have 'completely flipped,' steeper Phillips curve
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller signaled a hawkish pivot, noting risks have 'completely flipped' from 2024-25 labor market concerns to rising inflation after 9 months of consistent overshoot in a stabilizing labor market. He questioned explicit forward guidance effectiveness and cited Boston Fed research showing price shocks now transmit multiple times larger impacts to sticky prices than pre-COVID — relevant for rate trajectory and growth/tech valuations.

bullets.title: MSFT corporate access: Morgan Stanley Media & Comms day Aug 11 — CHTR, ROKU, T, VZ, LYV, TKO, OMC, PSKY
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley hosting in-person 1x1s with CHTR, LYV, OMC, PSKY, ROKU, TKO, T, and VZ management on August 11 at 1585 Broadway. 1x1 booking deadline is Friday July 10th.
